To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary restriction, insulin and the insulin-lowerer diazoxide all have the potential to reduce the incidence and/or growth of cancer.

1) dietary restriction reduces insulin/IGF levels, which reduces cancer growth and improves response to chemotherapy, 2) insulin administration reduces cancer growth and increases sensitivity to chemotherapy, 3) diazoxide lowers insulin levels, and thus may reduce the growth of cancer cells and improve sensitivity to chemotherapy.
dietary restriction of calories and macronutrients can reduce cancer incidence, growth and metastasis, and that these effects may depend on the insulin/IGFs system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the insulin/IGFs can be manipulated to achieve the best results in cancer treatment.
the question whether dietary and pharmacological modification can be exploited to improve the efficacy of anticancer therapy.
a broad spectrum of approaches that may be useful in cancer treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the full repertoire of dietary and pharmacological modifications of the insulin-IGF-1 axis has to be exploited against cancer.
the insulin/IGFs system is a key regulator of metabolism and cancer, and that it is therefore a promising target for cancer treatment.
the use of dietary or pharmacological modification of insulin and IGF-1 levels in cancer treatment has to be further evaluated in clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary restriction is an effective strategy for cancer prevention and therapy.
dietary restriction is a very promising strategy to prevent and treat cancer.
dietary restriction, insulin and diazoxide are all able to reduce the incidence of cancer and/or the growth of cancer cells in animal models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the insulin/IGT-1 system is a promising therapeutic target for cancer, and that dietary restriction and pharmacological manipulation of insulin levels may be useful strategies to achieve this.

we should not be afraid of using the full repertoire of dietary and pharmacological interventions in cancer patients, but we need to be aware of the potential side effects and interactions with other drugs.

dietary and pharmacological manipulation of the insulin/ IGF-1 system has great potential to improve the outcome of anticancer treatment, and that it may also provide new treatment options for patients who do not respond to conventional therapies.
